# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Clock Struck One" by Fergus Hume (1898, Warne; Gutenberg 55689)

**Characters**
- **Dora Carew**: heroine, tall, gold curls, grey eyes, rides bicycle; ward of Julian Edermont; 21; £500/yr "inheritance" was a lie. Engaged to Allen Scott.
- **Allen (Dr. Allen) Scott**: young doctor in Canterbury; son of Dr. Scott (killed 20+ yrs ago at Christchurch by Captain George Carew). Nurse/housekeeper Mrs. Tice.
- **Julian Edermont** (real name **Julian Dargill**): recluse, Red House near Chillum, Canterbury; small, white hair, silvery beard; fears violent death; Litany prayer "From battle and murder, and from sudden death, good Lord, deliver us." Murdered night of 2/3 Aug, head smashed by Zulu knobkerrie.
- **Lambert Joad**: drunk, lecherous, ~60, ex-clergyman, Edermont's friend; lives in cottage across road; "Silenus"; in love with Dora; secretly the one who put clock an hour fast, stole manuscript.
- **Lady Laura Burville** (born Laura Treherne; "L.B." pearl brooch): Dora's mother; married (1) Captain George Carew, (2) Dargill, (3) Sir John Burville. Staying at Hernwood Hall with Sir Harry Hernwood. Address: No. 22 Jersey Place, Mayfair.
- **Augustus Pallant**: red-haired, blue-eyed blackmailer; told Edermont Carew was dead (fear ended); blackmailed Laura; later shot in San Francisco.
- **Mr. Pride** (John Mallison): chubby tutor at Chillum school; real murderer; Edermont's old friend who saved him from Carew.
- **Mrs. Tice**: Allen's old nurse, now housekeeper; knew Edermont/Carew history; husband died 25 yrs ago.
- **Meg Gance**: cook/servant at Red House; clock "an hour fast."
- **Inspector Jedd**: Canterbury police; wrong "tramp burglar" theory.
- **Dr. Chambers**: Canterbury doctor; time of death between 12 and 1.
- **Mr. Carver**: lawyer, Mercery Lane, Canterbury; executor; misogynist.
- **Captain George Theophilus Carew**: Dora's real father; violent; died San Francisco (Pallant present).
- **Dr. Scott (Allen's father)**: shot by Carew at Christchurch in mistake for Dargill.

**Sequence**
1. July noon, Dora on bridge 2 miles from Canterbury; meets Allen. Allen was called to treat Lady Burville (fainted in church). Edermont fainted at Litany when he saw her at Chillum Church.
2. At Red House: Joad admits them; Edermont (window) shrieks "He will kill me"; Allen flees.
3. Edermont warns Dora off Lady Burville; refuses explanation; "your parents sinned."
4. Dora to Canterbury; Mrs. Tice evasive; photo of Edermont (clean-shaven).
5. Pallant visits Edermont ("good news"); Edermont faints with joy; Pallant: "Beware of Allen Scott!"
6. 2 Aug night: Edermont wrote to Allen (midnight meeting) and to Laura. Dora hears cry, clock strikes one. Morning: Meg finds body.
7. Inquest: murder at ~1 a.m.; Joad's alibi (with Pride till after 2). Will: Edermont leaves £50,000 to whoever punishes his murderer; Red House + £200/yr to Dora on condition Joad stays.
8. Carver: no £500/yr exists; Dora nearly penniless (~"£8,000" claim false).
9. Mrs. Tice moved into Red House. Joad proposes; threatens: Allen was there at midnight, Joad saw him. Dora takes pearl brooch (found by Allen in study) to Lady Burville.
10. Allen's account: met a woman (Lady Burville) on bicycle near Chillum; fixed her puncture; found brooch.
11. Lady Burville's story: she visited Edermont ~11:30–12 for letters; Edermont alive when she left; "Carew killed Dargill."
12. Mrs. Tice's story: Carew shot Dr. Scott by mistake, Dargill's trap, Christchurch, 20+ yrs.
13. Dora finds clock "an hour fast" (Meg); searches Joad's cottage; finds "The Confession of Julian Dargill" in fireplace ashes.
14. Joad confronts Dora; drinks; goes to Carver.
15. Manuscript reveals: Dora is Dargill's daughter, not Carew's; Allen's father's killer is not her father.
16. Confession: Joad confessed to Carver (Joad had heard Edermont's letter; hid in hall, put clock back; stole manuscript from desk; Mallison/Pride came; Mallison killed Edermont with knobkerrie after Edermont pulled pistol; Mallison forced Joad to silence; Joad alibied via cottage at 1).
17. Ending: Joad dies of heart attack on doorstep the night Pride arrested (Meg's clock evidence + Joad's confession); Mallison hanged, confessed at last. Pallant shot in San Francisco. Laura remarried Burville. Joad's will leaves £50,000 to Dora. Dora marries Allen in spring; house left; Carver ("misogamist").

**Key clues**: clock an hour fast; pearl brooch "L.B."; manuscript in fireplace; Christchurch; 22 Jersey Place; 1 a.m. chime; postern gate open; Litany prayer.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Case of the Black Twenty-Two" by Brian Flynn (1929, Grosset & Dunlap; Gutenberg 75209)

**Characters**
- **Peter Daventry**: junior partner, "Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry, Solicitors," Cornhill, London; Oxford man; brother Gerald (Wedderburn & Rathbone accountants).
- **David Linnell**: senior partner, 58, Lancashire-born, shrewd.
- **Plunkett**: 35-year clerk.
- **Laurence P. Stewart**: American millionaire, Assynton Lodge, Berkshire (near Wantage); collector obsessed with Mary, Queen of Scots relics; murdered 8 June (night).
- **Charles Stewart**: son, ~22.
- **Colonel Leach-Fletcher**: "Neuve Chapelle" bungalow, near Rockinge; dined with Stewart night of murder.
- **Marjorie Lennox**: ward, "M. L."; petite, blue eyes, retroussé nose; lied about being in library.
- **Morgan Llewellyn**: secretary, reddish-brown eyes, pince-nez; love letter to Marjorie threatening; "M. L." note's initials not his.
- **John Butterworth**: butler, 60+, ex-service of Sir Julian Kennedy; wife housekeeper; **the murderer of Stewart**.
- **Alice Mortimer** (née Butterworth) with husband "Snoop" Mortimer (alias Laurence C. Stewart II; "Flash Alf"; New York crook); hotel Blanchard's, Clifford Street; Regent 9999; Alice hay-fever, dark glasses.
- **Patrick O'Connor**: boot-boy, 18; bicycle used by murderer; father **Michael O'Connor**, foundry giant with black beard.
- **Maidment**: gardener.
- **Sergeant Clegg**: local police, Assynton.
- **Detective-Inspector Goodall**: Scotland Yard.
- **Anthony Bathurst**: amateur detective, Uppingham, ex-Oxford; solves case.
- **Forshaw (Ronald)**, **Day**, **Palmers**: auction house Day, Forshaw & Palmers, Hanover Galleries.
- **Druce**: night-watchman, 6 years; **James (Jim) Mason**: night-watchman murdered (skull, 4 blows).
- **Mrs. Turner**: cleaner.
- **Andrew Ferguson** of Crake & Ferguson, New York; Stewart's solicitors.
- **Rosemary Armitage** of The Towers (Charles's fiancée).
- **Marriott**: friend at Violette restaurant.
- **Mr. Lironi**: Violette proprietor.
- **Rabjohns**: chambermaid, Blanchard's; **Atkins**: porter.

**Sequence**
1. June 1928-ish (dates "June 7th"; sale June 10 at 1 p.m.). Stewart letter instructs Linnell's firm to buy: No. 37 Collar of Pearls, No. 38 Antique Tapestry Fire-screen, No. 39 Rosary of Amber Beads, "property of Mary, Queen of Scots," from Lord Clavering's sale (Day, Forshaw & Palmers, Hanover Galleries).
2. At the Violette, Peter (lunching) says aloud "So's Mary, Queen of Scots"; man at next table (with woman) knocks cruet over; woman's look; couple talk "let's go to-morrow — not to-day."
3. Peter views items; two plain-clothes men present; screen motto beads "JESUS CHRIST, GOD AND SAVIOUR"; corners: Scots Lion, fleur-de-lis, Leopards and Lilies.
4. Linnell telegrams Stewart; reply "Say what the hell's biting you—when I say Buy—then Buy. Got that? Stewart."
5. Night of 9/10 June: Mason murdered; Hanover Galleries robbed; items 37, 38, 39 stolen. Woman asked Druce the way to Marble Arch (sneezed). Mason and Druce distracted; murderer picked lock of Day's office, pounced on Mason.
6. Linnell learns; Peter phoned: Stewart murdered in Assynton library, head battered.
7. Assynton: library door locked from inside, French doors bolted. Stewart at desk, note "Urgent in the morning! M. L." Revolver in left dressing-gown pocket, one chamber fired. Stewart last seen by Butterworth ~10 p.m.; Llewellyn last saw him at dinner; Charles came in ~9:45, Colonel present.
8. Clegg finds lady's handkerchief "M. L." in curtains. Marjorie denies being in library; accuses Llewellyn ("Morgan Llewellyn!").
9. Butterworth: heard Stewart and a woman's voice (Marjorie) in library ~10:10 p.m.
10. Trunk-call from library-area phone to Blanchard's Hotel, 11 minutes; "Mr. and Mrs. Laurence Charles Stewart" left hastily.
11. Bathurst (with Peter) travel by 6:55 from Paddington with Goodall. Bathurst deduces: murderer used O'Connor's bicycle (tar on tyres); Bathurst deduces stone weapon thrown in rockery pool; bullet found in *The Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure* in bookcase.
12. Llewellyn's letter to Marjorie found in Renan's *Vie de Jésus*.
13. Stuart secret: Greek "ICHTHUS" fish; Latin "Timeo Danaos" (on metal screen); fish conceals hidden cavity; 22 Black Pearls of Lorraine (Cardinal of Lorraine's gift; "Black Twenty-Two"; Thibaut Girardier, armorer).
14. Ferguson arrives; will: £250,000 to Marjorie and residue to Charles, conditional on marrying each other. Anthony gets Charles to close house. Final night: Butterworth and "Mortimer" in library with both screens; arrested by Goodall. Pearls recovered. Charles's wedding gift idea for Marjorie.

**Key clues**: "M. L." initials (Merryweather, Linnell & Daventry); Virgil; Ichthus; hay fever; Mason's three knocks; pool stone; bullet in book (848 pages).
